** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Discard stale refresh responses before updating the list.** An all-window scan can finish after a newer current-window scan. This assignment then replaces the current-window results with all-window results. The current-window indicator stays active, and the master action can move tabs from other windows. Assign each refresh a generation number. Apply a response only if its generation and requested scope are still current.

Review comment at @popup/popup.js at line 313: Prevent stale refresh responses from replacing newer tab results. In the refresh flow around the currentTabs assignment, assign each refresh a generation number and apply response.tabs only when that generation is still current and the requested scope still matches the active scope; preserve the existing empty-list fallback for accepted responses. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Block resubmission of tab IDs that an active batch still owns.** The master button is disabled during a batch at `popup/popup.js:330`. A later render calls `updateSelectionUI`, which enables the button again whenever the selection is not empty (`popup/tab-list.js:60-67`). A second click then sends the same tab IDs in a new `MOVE_TABS` request. The background does not prevent this. `moveTabsThrottled` (`background/tab-mover.js:174-188`) handles each ID independently and tracks no IDs in progress. Two overlapping requests can call `moveOrReuseTab` for the same tab. The second call can start before the first call finishes with that tab. Required behaviour: one tab ID must not be processed by two batches at the same time. Use one of these approaches: - Keep the master action disabled while a batch is active, even after a re-render. - Track in-flight tab IDs in the background and skip IDs that another request already owns. The background check protects against duplicate processing even when the popup sends an overlapping request.

Release each ID from the in-flight set when its processing completes, including on failure, so later batches can process it. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Continue initialisation if configuration loading fails.** If this message rejects, the callback exits before `refreshTabs(true)`. The popup does not scan automatically, although manual Refresh remains available. Catch the rejection, retain `currentConfig` defaults, and continue initialisation. Keep applying stored values when the request succeeds.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Load installed-app metadata before the first grouped render.** At this point, `installedApps` is still empty. Only the Settings workflow populates it. An installed app that covers multiple domains therefore appears as separate host groups until the user opens Settings. Fetch `GET_INSTALLED_APPS` before the initial render. Keep an empty-array fallback if discovery fails.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Make each group accordion keyboard-operable.** The group header is a `div` with only a click handler. Keyboard users cannot focus it or expand one group without using Expand All. Add a separate native toggle button with `aria-expanded`. Keep the checkbox and Open Group button outside that toggle.
